name: East Greenland Coastal Current
scope: Declared southeast Greenland coastal study-area reach from an OSW offshore gate near 66 N to a Cape Farewell offshore gate near 60 N. Excludes the weak northern 68 N identification, EGC shelfbreak path, Irminger Current, offshore diversions and West Greenland continuation. Not the full EGCC or the source-reported approximately 1000 km surveyed shelf. Near 63 N, the coastal and shelfbreak flows approach or merge; the line does not establish uninterrupted independent coastal flow. The local 30 km Cape Farewell width is not a buffer around this reach.
layer: Surface-intensified low-salinity inner-shelf jet context from July-August 2004 hydrography and ADCP-referenced geostrophic velocity. No uniform fixed-depth axis diagnosed along this editorial path.
time_convention: Editorial regional geography informed by the July-August 2004 JR105 campaign. Not a simultaneous measured axis, annual mean or recurring summer footprint.
source_locator: Sutherland and Pickart (2008), section 3: Cape Farewell and 66 N section geography; section 3.5: weak assumed northern jet near 68 N; sections 8-9: merging near 63 N and approximately 1000 km shelf survey description. Relevant text inspected, no current-axis figure digitized.
source_citation: Sutherland and Pickart (2008), The East Greenland Coastal Current: Structure, variability, and forcing, Progress in Oceanography, accepted manuscript.
source_license: WHOI-hosted accepted manuscript; no explicit reuse license inspected. Attributed geographic facts paraphrased; source figures and velocity fields are not copied.
coordinate_selection: OSW selects coarse offshore vertices following the southeast Greenland coastal sequence. Gates near 66 N and Cape Farewell are editorial truncations, not observed current origin/termination. Surface fresh-water wedges alone do not diagnose the jet. The 63 N merger is retained as a scope warning, not an invented separate uninterrupted branch. Coarse land avoidance does not establish inner-shelf placement. Initial southern scenarios touched the coarse land mask; the Cape Farewell approach gate was moved east to 42.9 W before regeneration. This clearance is not bathymetric validation.

alternative_routes.interpretation: OSW coarse lateral alternative; not an observed axis, current edge or width.
OSW coarse lateral alternative; not an observed axis, current edge or width.

scenario_rule: Three editorial offshore reach shapes crossed with uniform longitude shifts -0.1/0/+0.1 degrees and independent endpoint latitude shifts -0.1/0/+0.1 degrees: 81 scenarios. Neither an annual range nor a confidence interval.
remaining_gates: Review finer coastline and shelf bathymetry before claiming an inner-shelf current axis.
Resolve northern identification and the 63 N merger before any whole-current extent.
Do not replace the source approximately 1000 km shelf survey description with this shorter editorial reach.
Retain the Cape Farewell 30 km threshold width as a local section; no width buffer or annual footprint inferred.
